tasks.title: Protected forms accept bounded list fields and shared writes support incident and maintenance audit targets
tasks.spec: ## Repository: console, contract pin, shared infrastructure in Behavior and unit Checks; Required behavior 1-3 (dispatcher, list fields, body limits and ApiCall), 10-11 (shared sender and People targets); Security impact (auth order, body limits and dependency pins). Pin contract to c4a2eb5214d48d40d0c1afbae5e3e49463185e15 or a later full main SHA containing 2.3.0 and regenerate bun.lock. Add optional ProtectedRoute.listFields and required PageRequest.lists, empty on GET/HEAD. Thread list parsing through the existing readFormFields/readPostForm pipeline in src/http-context.ts and protected dispatcher in src/server.ts; preserve callers without list fields and the fixed POST order. Add the two form limits, reject duplicate list values and over-limit counts, and never allow csrf/form_token as lists. Add the four ApiCall names and seven PeopleAction values and the incident/maintenance target encodings from section 11. Export/generalize the check sender and People-row helper with per-resource texts, optional revision and resource identifiers, keeping existing check write behavior and tests green. Update the existing PageRequest literal in token-write.test.ts with empty lists so the typecheck stays green at this step. This task supplies shared support only; resource-specific routes, outcome policies and calls follow in T2/T3. Update configuration docs for list-field validation and limits. The existing shared POST pipeline and regression suites are supporting paths beyond the plan's Files list, required to carry lists without duplicating the security checks. Request counting: shared dispatcher refusals stop before the handler (0 reads and 0 writes); live write guards run after handler reads and prohibit only writes. Preserve the existing gate-based testing pattern in server.checks-write.test.ts for the new route tests in T2/T3. The 32768-byte incident form bound accommodates title 200 and message 2000 Unicode code points of four UTF-8 bytes each, plus 50 component ids and hidden fields (about 30650 URL-encoded bytes); this transport bound must not become a UTF-16 text-length rule.

tasks.title: People can inspect, publish, update, resolve and delete incidents with a live status-card preview
tasks.spec: ## Repository: console, incident portion of Behavior, Fake API, Checks and Docs; Required behavior 1-10, incident portion of 11 and 14; incident Counterexamples through Private filtering; Acceptance evidence 1-2, 4-9, 11-12, plus the incident half of 10 (browser round trips). Implement the complete incident feature on T1's shared support: bounded public-only reads, first-failure states, 404-as-empty manual list, list filters/order/200-row bound, separate MTTR populations and duration formatting, manual timelines and read-only automatic detail/results, composer and automatic shortcut, post update, resolve and typed-title delete. Register exact raw-path protected routes and roles, validate query ids and set incident navId; both navigation entries are enabled together in final T3 after both page families exist. Normalize CRLF in messages without trimming title/message, validate components, route/JSON byte limits and bodies with the pinned contract, and implement every section 10 outcome. Text lengths follow the contract's code-point behavior: add no String.length check or maxlength. Cover every literal Contract length row, including mixed emoji and the 201-emoji title. Add isUntitledIncident in incident-form.ts using !/[\p{L}\p{N}\p{P}\p{S}]/u.test(title). An untitled title is shown as Untitled incident #<id> in list links, detail headings/page titles, resolve and delete pages; preview and API bodies retain raw text. For deletion derive the confirm name from the incident read: Incident <id> for untitled titles, otherwise the raw title. Use shipped typedNameError/isTypedNameConfirmed with trim/NFC behavior; keep confirm.ts and its tests unchanged. The composer refuses new untitled titles with the literal section 9 error, 422, input kept, one read and zero writes. Keep the known revision field equal to update count on delete, without a POST revision comparison. Every write is guarded immediately before its one outbound request; incidents send no If-Match, retry or followed redirect, and log only section 11 identities/outcomes. Compose the resolve page in incident-pages.ts with existing html.ts field/error/button helpers. Two open resolve GETs issue independent tokens; already-resolved update/resolve POSTs keep text and give 409 after two reads and zero writes; a resolution race shows API 409 after one write. Implement escaped server preview and independent textContent live preview in the sole existing console script, unchanged CSP, one delegated input/change listener, no request/storage/timer; resolved preview shows all updates and open preview only the latest. Add the stateful manual-incident fake with contract validation, auth, ordered {method,path} request recording and parsed JSON write-body recording, gated read replies for role/session changes, the 100-update limit, private-item switch and resolve-after-read switch. Permit seeding any contract-valid title, including whitespace and U+200B, as an incident created outside the console; seed independently of the composer. Also permit automatic incidents with any contract-valid checkId, including '.' and '..'. Reuse it in HTTP/browser fixtures and extend it for maintenance in T3. Add unit/HTTP/browser tests and incident docs here: mobile/axe/focus, JS/server preview parity, no-JS flows, code-point limits and untitled delete confirmation. Map every incident row of Request counting to a test asserting ordered read paths and separate write counts, including success, preview and refusal. No read follows a write. Only dispatcher refusals require zero API requests; handler refusals retain their specified reads and require zero writes. Use apiIdSegment for automatic-detail results paths; when undefined for check '.' or '..', make no results request, reuse the exported unaddressableText without changing check-detail-pages.ts, and return the otherwise complete 200 detail after only the automatic-list/config reads. Preserve the encoded query check link and from= preselection by exact check-id equality. In src/html.ts, put one literal LF immediately after textareaField's opening tag and before its escaped value; update its existing escape test and add the leading-LF literal in src/html.test.ts. Composer, update and resolve use textareaField for messages; preview messages use p elements, never pre/textarea. In Chromium with JavaScript disabled, fill a leading-LF message, preview and then publish the re-rendered composer and post-update forms; assert the actual fake-api write bodies retain the exact message. This task owns the lossless textarea helper change together with those incident browser regressions. Required behavior's shell rule and Acceptance evidence 12 apply to all incident no-form states. Do not change the shell or suppress its Sign out form/token. For the resolved GET /incidents/resolve response, slice the actual main element with id main, allowing its existing class attribute as in server.security.test.ts:782-784: inside main require 0 <form and 0 name="form_token"; in the whole body require 0 action="/incidents/resolve", exactly 1 name="form_token" and exactly 1 action="/sign-out". The resolved detail page has no action="/incidents/update" and no resolve link; its only form/token is still Sign out. Check the same absence rule for the other incident states that the spec says have no screen form. Token counts come from the unchanged shell in src/shell.ts:99-103 and signedInPage in src/server.ts:357-372, not incident rendering code. Never assert zero tokens across the whole signed-in page.

tasks.title: People can plan and manage durable maintenance windows and both screen families pass final evidence checks
tasks.spec: ## Repository: console, maintenance portion of Behavior and Fake API, navigation Checks, maintenance and whole-change Checks, Docs and Completion evidence; Required behavior 1-3 and 11-14; maintenance Counterexamples (Time parse through Phase boundary); Performance impact, Security impact, Rollout order 1 and Acceptance evidence 1-12. Build the Maintenance list, phase/source/shadowed views and all role-aware actions; create/edit with coherent maintenance/config revisions (one retry only), immutable id on edit, direct-check plus component selection snapshot, UTC round-trip parsing and unchanged millisecond preservation from the edit POST's own GET /admin/maintenance, contract validation, If-Match and maintenance-specific outcomes; delete database/shadowed copies with existing plainConfirmPage fields only. Enforce guards, list/body/JSON limits, stale input retention with zero window writes, unknown handling without retry and id-only People rows/logs. Extend T2's stateful fake with database/file/shadowed windows, injected phases, common revision and the exact API status semantics listed in Fake API, arbitrary stored epochs (including start 1793959200123), all-request and parsed-write-body recording and gated replies. For edit POST, always read /admin/maintenance then /admin/config before revision comparisons; both must equal the posted revision. Obtain original start/end only from windows[] source database with id equal to target, never from /admin/config or posted/hidden epochs. After those 2 reads, stale revision, shadowed/file-only target or missing target prevents all writes; no POST read retry. Read failure stops with the section 3 failure state. A forged shadowed/file-only edit is refused by the console precheck, not sent to the API. Register maintenance routes and enable both Incidents and Maintenance navigation entries together for every role; leave only Activity/System unavailable. Add maintenance unit/HTTP/browser tests beside implementation and extend fixture --serve for the complete manual journey. Finish docs, full suite/browser checks, required existing deploy-dev Compose job evidence, agent-browser lifecycle/mobile record and local-api smoke. The final security/evidence review covers all of T1-T3, including earlier incident tests and the maximum four API requests for the maintenance form retry. No API/contract/status product changes and no changes to confirm.ts or CSP. Map Acceptance evidence 6 to one HTTP test per row of Request counting (incident rows from T2 and maintenance rows here); separate total API requests, GET reads and mutations throughout tests, docs and PR evidence. The maximum remains 4 requests for a maintenance form GET retry; an edit POST has 2 reads plus at most 1 write. Include gated role-lowered/session-removed maintenance edit refusals after 2 reads and before any write. Final review includes T2's code-point and untitled-title unit/HTTP evidence (Acceptance evidence 9), including titles seeded independently of the composer. The maintenance note retains its separate 1-500 UTF-16-unit contract rule; do not apply the incident code-point rule to it. docs/incidents.md records code-point limits, untitled display/Incident <id> confirmation and the contract-comment risk; docs/maintenance.md records the note's UTF-16 limit. Time keep compares parsed whole-second epochs, never posted strings with prefills: for start and end independently, retain the stored epoch only if parsed === stored - (stored % 1000), otherwise use parsed. Test every Time keep Counterexamples row, including Chromium's omitted zero seconds, unchanged start AND end milliseconds, the changed second and the previous second. Add real Chromium maintenance edit submissions with JavaScript on and off, asserting the actual recorded PUT body rather than a helper's return value. This task owns the maintenance half of Acceptance evidence 10; final evidence also reruns T2's no-JS leading-LF preview-to-publish cases and its unaddressable automatic-detail cases (evidence 11). Apply Required behavior's shell rule to the maintenance no-form states (old-api Maintenance, shadowed/file-only edit, and stale form after the revision retry): inside the actual main element require 0 <form and 0 name="form_token"; whole body retains exactly 1 name="form_token" and 1 action="/sign-out", and 0 occurrences of that screen's own form action. Final evidence reruns T2's resolved GET /incidents/resolve 409 assertions with exactly those main-only absence and whole-body Sign out counts (Acceptance evidence 12). Keep shell.ts and the Sign out form/token issuance unchanged.
